title: Pattern Headings: Comics and Graphic Novels
scope: Free-floating period, author-group, topical, and form subdivisions for use under headings for individual genres and forms of comics and graphic novels, including Comic books, strips, etc.; pattern heading Biographical comic books, strips, etc.
pattern_category: individual genres and forms of comics and graphic novels, including Comic books, strips, etc.
general_notes: Headings for individual genres and forms of comics and graphic novels, including the general heading Comic books, strips, etc. Restrictions are noted in each section. Examples: Biographical comic books, strips, etc.; Graphic novels; Manga (Comic books); Romance comic books, strips, etc.

Comics and graphic novels are considered to be a form that includes both the written word and visual art. Therefore, the free-floating subdivisions in this instruction sheet are drawn from pattern headings for art (H 1148) and literature (H 1156).

Period subdivisions are listed first, author groups second, and topical and form subdivisions last, which is the proper order for considering these elements when formulating subject headings about particular themes in comics and graphic novels.

Headings for comics and graphic novels -- including the heading Comic books, strips, etc. -- may be subdivided geographically. Headings with geographic subdivisions may be further subdivided by topical and form subdivisions from section F and G below. Period and author group subdivisions from section D and section E below may not be combined in a single heading with geographic subdivisions. Instead, assign additional headings to bring out those aspects. [Section letters as printed; they refer to the topical/form sections G and H and the period/author group sections E and F.]
Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file.

Period subdivisions may be followed by topical and form subdivisions from section G and H below, with the noted exceptions, but may not be combined with author group subdivisions from section F below, nor used after headings for comics or graphic novels with geographic subdivision. If there are specific headings where these subdivisions are not appropriate, establish the appropriate subdivision under the specific heading.

Author group subdivisions may be followed by any topical or form subdivision from section G and H below but may not be combined in a single heading with period subdivisions from section E above nor used after headings with geographic subdivisions. Following this pattern, establish new subdivisions for national, ethnic, or religious groups only. Establish new subdivisions under the pattern heading for literature and for comics and graphic novels. For other author groups, follow the pattern of the phrase headings, Children’s writings, English--[place] or Prisoners’ writings, French--[place].

Subdivisions for religious author groups are used for comics and graphic novels written by authors who are members of the group, whether or not the comic or graphic novel includes religious themes. For example, assign Comic books, strips, etc.--Christian authors to comics or graphic novels by Christians. Comics and graphic novels with religious themes are entered under phrase headings for the genre, for example, Christian comic books, strips, etc.

Use the free-floating topical subdivisions listed in H 1148 and in H 1156, section G. These subdivisions may also be used under period subdivisions from section E above, or author group subdivisions from section F above with the noted exceptions. They may also be used after headings with geographic subdivision.

Use the free-floating form subdivisions listed in H 1148 and in H 1156, section H. These subdivisions may also be used under period subdivisions from section E above, or author group subdivisions from section F above with the noted exceptions. They may also be used after headings with geographic subdivision.

LC practice: As stated in H 1075, Library of Congress catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. To replace a form subdivision that includes a demographic group, also assign Library of Congress Demographic Group Terms (LCDGT) to bring out the audience of the resource being cataloged. The form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by LC catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.

The entry 'Film and video adaptations' (printed without a subfield code, with '--' in the geographic column) is a reference: see 'Film adaptations' and 'Television adaptations'; it is carried in this JSON with subfield "".
